SSB vs Mesa

Meta ads in India, snapshot 20 Nov 2026. SSB 30 ads, Mesa 249: SSB's are 30 of its 36 live ads, Mesa's 249 of about 320 from many views; not ranked by impressions. No spend or results are public.

Full-time PGP against PGP: Mesa puts a person to camera in 34 of its 67 PGP videos; you, 7 of 30. Your edge: the month-by-month timeline, 5 of 30.

Focus
  1. Open PGP ads on your own cohort outcomes, sourced.
    Mesa states a graduate outcome in 30 of its 93 PGP ads: 100% placements, a 25 lakh average, 58% founder-facing, 2.8x. Its figures conflict. None of your 30 gives a placement or salary figure.
    First test: Three 45-second cuts, each opening on one site figure with cohort and source: 19 LPA Cohort 1, 23 LPA Cohort 2, 40 placements.
    Strong evidence, low effortAdsScript
Start
  1. 1
    Answer Mesa's cohort call: seats, date, scholarships, aloud.
    Mesa's highest-scoring PGP idea is a 38-second cohort call, 9 ads and 16 versions: 200 people, the fifth cohort, "apply fast". None of your 30 names a scholarship or a live date.
    First test: Admissions lead to camera, 45 seconds: [seats], the admission page's next deadline, scholarships up to 100%, said and on the end card.
    Strong evidence, low effortAdsScript
  2. 2
    Make "By month 3" a series, speaker named with a role.
    Your highest-scoring idea: 5 ads, 7 versions, two shapes, day one on Bangalore streets to investors by month 6. The speaker has a name and no role; nothing is asked aloud.
    First test: Recut the square version: role under the name, "50 lakh" defined, a spoken close with seats, deadline and scholarships.
    Strong evidence, medium effortAdsScript
  3. 3
    Start PGP image ads; Mesa runs 26, you none.
    Mesa runs 26 image ads for its full-time PGP, 15 of them product or people across 11 ideas. None of your 30 sampled ads is an image; 6 live ads were not pulled.
    First test: Three image ads: a cohort CTC figure with source, a deadline and scholarships card, a still from the Mokobara project.
    Moderate evidence, low effortAds
Stop or fix
  1. 1
    Stop opening on "MBAs are outdated".
    11 of your 30 ads open by calling the MBA or college outdated, dead or not enough; 3 add an unsourced "one in four MBA graduates is unemployable". Your own rules say this backfires.
    First test: Recut the 3 "outdated" ads to open on "No CAT score needed", the site's line; keep the investor's middle.
    Strong evidence, low effortAdsScript
  2. 2
    Fix the passed date and the "MBA" wording.
    4 ads started 17 to 19 Nov still show "Early Bird Deadline 1st November 2026"; your site says 29 Nov. 29 ad texts say "MBA-equivalent PGP"; the site says certificate, not degree.
    First test: Today: drop the dated headline on 2 ads and the dated end card on 2; say "PGP in Management & Tech" in all ad text.
    In 8 adsAds

Full-time PGP: SSB walks a student month by month in 5 of its 30 ads; no PGP idea of yours does. Your edge: person to camera, 34 of 67 videos.

Focus
  1. Give the cohort call a spoken date and the site's seat count.
    Your highest-scoring PGP idea, 9 ads and 16 versions, calls for 200 people for the fifth cohort and ends "apply fast" with no date. Your site says 175 seats.
    First test: Recut the square cohort call: "175 seats", the Round 1 date as the PGP page states it, then the end card.
    Strong evidence, low effortAdsScript
Start
  1. 1
    Walk one student through the year, month by month.
    SSB's highest-scoring idea runs as 5 ads and 7 versions: day one on Bangalore streets, a D2C brand by month 3, investors by month 6. No PGP idea of yours walks the year in steps.
    First test: One PGP student to camera, 42 seconds: week 1, week 8, month [n], each with footage and the student's own figures.
    Strong evidence, medium effortAdsScript
  2. 2
    Name the investor and your staff on screen.
    Your investor recording runs as 11 ads in two edits, one opening on "200 plus startups", one on 5 lakhs in 8 weeks; he is never named on screen.
    First test: Add a name and role card in the first 3 seconds of the 8 cold-open ads, with his written consent.
    Strong evidence, low effortAdsScript
  3. 3
    Test one Hinglish cut.
    SSB's Hinglish endorsement runs as 3 ads and 5 versions; all 126 of your videos are in English.
    First test: A Hinglish cut of the careers lead's placement answer, 40 seconds, captions in Roman script.
    Moderate evidence, low effortAds
Stop or fix
  1. 1
    Settle one count per claim across your ads.
    Startups hiring from you are 100, 150 or 500 by ad; one student brand does 20 or 25 lakh a month; the 5 lakh line has no stated scope.
    First test: Take the placement report's figure for each and recut the careers-lead, khakra and salary-rise videos first.

Workhorses

What they lean on

Counting ads per row hides that one idea or one series can carry a brand. Here are the ideas each brand keeps re-running. Long life and many versions are a sign a brand keeps paying for an idea, not that it performs.

You spread 30 ads over 11 ideas: the timeline film carries 5 (17%), the three largest 12 (40%). Mesa's full-time PGP leans on the cohort call (9 ads) and one investor recording (11 ads); half of all Mesa's ads, 127 of 249, sell its part-time Ascend.

In your 93 full-time PGP ads the cohort call carries 9 (10%), the three largest 24 (26%). Across all 249, Ascend leads: 32 quit-your-job image cards and a 32-ad interview shoot. SSB's 30 ads sit on 11 ideas, led by its 5-ad timeline film.

Leaning score = ads using the idea + half a point per extra version + one point per 30 days of its longest-running ad + 2 points per extra product, city or centre it is re-cut for (places as named in each ad's text). For the content team

Scripts to brief

Each direction is one line you can say to the team, then the detail to brief it. Figures in [brackets] are yours to fill from the live product on the day of the edit; every other fact is taken from the brands' own ads or sites.

1Proof first: open on one cohort's average CTC, with its source on screenProgramme or careers lead to camera, vertical, phone or one-camera set, cut to real campus footage for the proof beat; 45 seconds; English

Who it talks to. 22 to 27, a graduate or 1 to 3 years into a job, weighing an MBA, who wants proof of placement before anything else.

Why. Mesa states a graduate outcome in 30 of its 93 PGP ads (100% placements, a 25 lakh average, 58%, 2.8x, named alumni roles). None of your 30 ads gives a placement or salary figure, though your site lists 19 and 23 LPA by cohort. ad 1, ad 2, ad 3, ad 4

First 3 seconds, options

  • Scaler School of Business. Our first cohort's average CTC: 19 LPA.
  • Cohort 1 averaged 19 LPA. Cohort 2 is at 23. Here's what they did.
  • 40 placements and 5 founders, from our very first batch.

Beats

0-3 sHandoffBrand and the strongest proof in the first line; the figure with its cohort.
3-12 sProblemThe problem, without running down the MBA.
12-15 sBridgeOne-line pivot.
15-22 sProduct specsFormat, length, place, operators who built companies.
22-31 sExperiential proofNamed company project, set up first.
31-38 sCredibility stackTenure, distribution, second cohort outcome.
38-45 sCall to actionScarcity, deadline, incentive, one action.

Draft script

TimeVoiceOn screen
0-3 sScaler School of Business. Our first cohort's average CTC: 19 LPA.Big text "19 LPA avg. CTC, Cohort 1" with "Source: [SSB placement report]". Lower-third: [speaker name], [role], SSB.
3-12 sEvery recruiter asks the same question. Not where you studied. What have you actually built, sold or shipped? Most graduates have read about business. Few have done it.Caption: "What have you actually built?"
12-15 sAt SSB, you build from week one.Cut to students at a market stall.
15-22 s18 months, full time, on our Bengaluru campus. Taught by CEOs, CMOs and product heads, with mentors from Zomato and Razorpay.Text: "18 months | Full time | Bengaluru".
22-31 sYou run a live D2C brand with a ₹5 lakh revenue target in 6 weeks, and build go-to-market plans for brands like Mokobara, presented to the founders.Real footage of the D2C stall and the Mokobara session; caption "₹5L+ target in 6 weeks".
31-38 sScaler has been in education since 2016, with 1,200+ hiring partners. And Cohort 2's current average CTC? 23 LPA.Text: "1,200+ hiring partners" / "23 LPA current avg. CTC, Cohort 2" with its source.
38-45 s[Seats] seats. Applications close [next deadline]. Scholarships up to 100%. Apply now, link below.End card: "PGP in Management & Tech", [seats] seats, "Apply by [next deadline]", "Scholarships up to 100%*".

On-screen notes. Every figure on screen with its cohort and source line; the speaker's name and role from the first second. No MBA comparison.

End card. SSB logo, "PGP in Management & Tech", "18-Month | Full-Time | Bangalore Campus", [seats] seats, "Apply by [next deadline]", "Scholarships up to 100%*", "*At the discretion of the Scaler Impact Foundation. Certificate programme."

Compliance watch-outs

  • Call it the PGP in Management & Tech, a certificate programme. Never "MBA", "degree" or "MBA students": SSB's site says it is not a university and does not confer degrees.
  • Every CTC or placement figure carries its cohort and source on screen ("19 LPA avg. CTC, Cohort 1", "23 LPA current avg. CTC, Cohort 2"). Scaler's online figures (5,000+ placed, 19 lakh median) are labelled as Scaler's online programmes, never as SSB's.
  • Scholarships are "up to 100%", with "awarded at the discretion of the Scaler Impact Foundation" on the end card.
  • One live deadline: the one on the admission page on the day of the edit (29 Nov 2026 on 22 Nov). Take a dated card down the day after it passes.
  • No "India's only" or "India's first" without a source on screen; pick one tagline for all ads.
  • Name every speaker with a role on screen; get written consent from students and from named companies (Mokobara, Zomato, Razorpay) before they appear.
  • No unsourced figures about other schools or their graduates ("one in four unemployable").

What to measure

  • Hold to 3 seconds and to 15 seconds against the square "By month 3" cut (your highest-scoring idea)
  • Form fills on the minimal landing page (all 30 sampled ads go there) and cost per form
  • Applications with the fee paid within 14 days of the form
  • Comments asking "is it an MBA?" or "what is the fee?", a sign of what the ad left unclear

Why. Mesa's highest-scoring PGP idea is a 38-second cohort call: 9 ads, 16 versions, "200 special people" for the fifth cohort. None of your 30 ads names a scholarship; "the next 100 students" is said only in the timeline film, and the only date shown has passed. ad 1, ad 2, ad 3

Why. Your highest-scoring idea: the timeline film runs as 5 ads and 7 versions in two shapes, from day one on Bangalore streets to investors by month 6. The speaker is captioned by name only, "50 lakh" is never defined, and nothing is asked aloud. ad 1, ad 2, ad 3

Compliance watch-outs

  • Call it the PGP in Management & Tech, a certificate programme. Never "MBA", "degree" or "MBA students": SSB's site says it is not a university and does not confer degrees.
  • Every CTC or placement figure carries its cohort and source on screen ("19 LPA avg. CTC, Cohort 1", "23 LPA current avg. CTC, Cohort 2"). Scaler's online figures (5,000+ placed, 19 lakh median) are labelled as Scaler's online programmes, never as SSB's.
  • Scholarships are "up to 100%", with "awarded at the discretion of the Scaler Impact Foundation" on the end card.
  • One live deadline: the one on the admission page on the day of the edit (29 Nov 2026 on 22 Nov). Take a dated card down the day after it passes.
  • No "India's only" or "India's first" without a source on screen; pick one tagline for all ads.
  • Name every speaker with a role on screen; get written consent from students and from named companies (Mokobara, Zomato, Razorpay) before they appear.
  • No unsourced figures about other schools or their graduates ("one in four unemployable").

Full script

By month 3 at SSB you'll have more experience than most MBA graduates. And now we're looking for the next 100 students. So years only year at SSB you would actually look like. And somewhere in between, you've learned more about business in the last two years that a class group could ever teach you. Traditional B schools will still be a number, creating graduates who all look the same on the table. But if you have got something to prove, this is the right place.

Full script

In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

Method

Method and limits

  • Sample. Meta ads in India, two pulls of very different size, so the page compares shares, not raw counts. SSB: 30 of the 36 ads live on its page on 20 Nov 2026 (UTC), from the Library's all-ads view in its own default order (not sorted by impressions); the first two tries of that view and one video-only view came back empty, and the last 6 ads were not pulled. All 30 are video; the sample holds no image ads. Mesa: 249 of about 320 live ads, pulled on 18 and 19 Nov 2026 through many views: all, video and image views sorted by total impressions high to low and low to high (30 ads each where they loaded), date windows and keyword searches (Ascend, MBA, salary, business, build, learn and others); several views came back empty. Mesa's sample is close to all its live ads, not a ranking. 8 of Mesa's 123 image ads have no tags file and are placed by programme from headline and landing page, in no row.
  • Snapshot. 20 November 2026. Ads live on that day only.
  • SSB. 30 ads: 30 video (16 distinct videos), 0 image. 0 could not be placed in a row; they count in the totals but in no row.
  • Mesa. 249 ads: 126 video (44 distinct videos), 123 image. 8 could not be placed in a row; they count in the totals but in no row.
  • No spend or results. The Ad Library does not publish spend, reach or results for these ads. We use what is public: which ads the Library shows first, how long each has run, and how many versions run. The default order is the Library's own and is not documented, so it is not a ranking by impressions or spend.
  • Shares. Video rows are shares of a brand's sampled video ads, image rows of its sampled image ads. The views were taken in the Library's default order, so the video and image split is whatever those views returned; a medium with under 10 ads on a side shows counts, not shares, and a side with none reads "none".
  • Days live are days so far: ads still running are counted to the snapshot date.
  • Versions are the Library's count of ads that share a creative. Mixed-format set-ups, where Meta combines images, videos and text, inflate it, so we lean on ideas, not versions.
  • Status rules. A brand is present in a row at 3 ads. Only: one side present. Leads: both present and a share at least 2 times the other's. Even: both present, under that. Evidence is strong at 8 ads across 3 ideas, thin under 4 ads or a single idea, moderate otherwise.
  • Founders. Counted only where the ad itself says founder, co-founder or CEO. Nobody is identified from a face.
  • Tag check, SSB. Not done yet.
  • Tag check, Mesa. Not done yet.
  • Scripts are typed by software and can mishear names and non-English words.

Here, students build GTM strategies for real brands like Mokobara, Southeast Asia launch, presenting their ideas, exactly to the founders. And somewhere in between, you've learned more about business in the last two years that a class group could ever teach you. Traditional B schools will still be a number, creating graduates who all look the same on the table. But if you have got something to prove, this is the right place.

At SSB, business isn’t taught in theory. It’s learned by working on company sourced projects, building AI products, and working with Industry operators. An MBA-equivalent PGP built for how business actually works today. Script: A lot of post graduates are probably doing jobs that are not compensated to their skills, to their ambitions and to whatever they've learnt. Access to the right content is not an issue. Students know what to study, where to study, when to study. The issue is converting that knowledge into what might be practical, filtered, applicable, daily work is where I think students are suffering. Learning hands-on and learning while doing is one of the biggest unlocks you can get because traditional education was about theoretical learning and then practicing it later on. I think schools like SSB schools which are kind of focusing on combining practiced business learnings with theoretical understanding of concepts are the ones where gap is getting bridged. If I were a student even at UH College like an SSB today, I do think that exposure would have helped.

Assuming that the premium market in India is large was one. Naming the brand in a very long way was the other. Making a logo and a brand identity that was not very suitable for packaging was a third. But in hindsight, I think each mistake to do something, it humbles you. Bombay Shwena Company is 11 years of two steps forward, one step back. And just the ability to survive through mistakes. I think we have learned from them. And institutions have the responsibility of channeling that. Sackord SSB is doing schools that teach entrepreneurship, teach kids to learn, entrepreneurship, while building and doing, are the ones who will create jobs in the future. There is a massive wave of schools like SSB, which is now kind of harnessing what I call the inspiration, aspiration, perspiration of a large number of young students in the right direction. If I was a student in a new age MBA college, black and SSB today, I do think that exposure would have helped.

“The actual efficient size of a company is shrinking very rapidly.”
Video ad, person to camera. 8 days live from 11 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Your classmates could be your co-founders From MNC managers to ex-founders to first-time builders. Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership is built for professionals who want to build, and make an impact. Apply now. Script: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Naval Ravi Khan. I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become the 10,001th employee in our MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95% of jobs in MNCs are going to be taken away by AI. And what that means is, theoretically speaking, there are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain. Either you become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Now, both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from zero to one, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product. And this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision making in startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. If you are somebody who's interested, then Mesa is still accepting applications. Apply as quickly as possible.

Be part of Mesa's next cohort 200 people. 12 months. 2000+ hours of hands-on, practical learning. At Mesa, you learn from 200+ founders and operators, solve 10+ real business problems, build real D2C businesses, and launch AI products to real paying users. PGP in Startup Leadership & Entrepreneurship. Apply now. Script: We are looking for 200 people who do not want to learn business the traditional way. Over the next 12 months, these 200 students will go through 2,000 plus hours of hands-on, practical learning, a curriculum designed by the startup ecosystem. You'll learn directly from 200 plus founders and operators, solve 10 plus real business problems from companies like head-out, blankets, snabbit and urban company. You will build a real D2C business from scratch, sell to real customers and generate over 5 lakh in revenue. You'll build AI products using tools like Claude, NETN, Resend, launch them on product hunt and get real paying users. If that's how you want to learn business, apply to my site.

“I spent two years preparing for UPSC.”
Video ad, person to camera. 4 days live from 15 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: customer. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Be part of Mesa's next cohort She started her career at KPMG and wanted to work in startups, but had no idea how to make the switch. At Mesa, Apoorva built an AI agent that could find influencers, track their engagement and automate personalised outreach. That agent led her to the founder of GoDesi. Today, she's an EiR at GoDesi, working directly with the founder. Script: I spent two years preparing for UPSC. Today, I work directly with the founder of a fast-growing F&B startup. I started my career at KPMG and then decided to join Mesa School of Business. I always wanted to work in the F&B industry, but I had no idea how to make that transition. During my 12 months at Mesa, I got to build two businesses of my own. Worked on dual business problems with two brothers' organic farms, where I worked on influencer marketing for the US market. And here's the interesting part. Before Mesa, I was someone who was genuinely scared of technology. But during my time at Mesa, I built an AI agent that could identify relevant influencers, track their engagement number, and automate personalized outreach. And this AI agent got me an interview with the founder of GoDacy. Today, I work as an AI at GoDacy, where I manage multiple product categories across quick commerce platforms. So, I'm preparing for UPSC to building AI automations and working directly with the startup founder. That's how much my career pivoted in just 12 months. If you're looking to make a similar career switch and work in high-impact roles at India's top startups, explore Mesa's 12-month PGP in startup leadership. Apply now!

“Only 0.001% of people have actually built something useful using AI.”
Video ad, person to camera. 3 days live from 16 Nov, 7 versions. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Non-tech doesn't mean non-builder AI is woven into every course at Mesa with 150+ hours of applied curriculum built around one goal: every student builds at least one real, working AI product before they graduate. Not a demo. Not a prototype. Something that actually works. The window to be an early builder, not just an early learner - is still open. Explore the PG program. Get the details. Script: Only 0.001% of people have actually built something useful using AI. And this is after knowing that AI is the number one skill to learn right now. Why is it that this gap is so massive? Because most people think it's too technical for them. Because there are thousands of tools and nobody knows what to use when. Because they watch tutorials, but they've never sat down to think about what should I do with those tutorials. And because even the few who start don't have anyone to guide them through the finish line. Mesa solves exactly this. AI isn't a separate module you'll learn. It's woven into every single course. 150 plus hours of applied AI curriculum. And every student builds at least one real AI product before they graduate. Not a demo, not a toy project, something that works. For example, one of our students, an investment banker with zero tech background. Built a vice-first AI companion, pitched it to 50 plus VCs, scaled it to 1000 plus monthly active users. Another one built an AI-powered tool that got him his dream job. Another pivoted entirely into AI, and is now leading an AI product at a fast growing startup. The gap right now isn't between people who understand AI and people who don't. It's between people who have built with AI and people who haven't. Mesa meets sure around the right side of that gap.

“The actual efficient size of a company is shrinking very rapidly.”
Video ad, person to camera. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The next decade belongs to builders Large companies are becoming leaner, AI is automating layers of work that used to require headcount, and a growing share of opportunity is concentrating inside small, high-leverage teams, i.e. startups. Most business programs was built for the old version of this economy: one with stable hierarchies, predictable career ladders, and large organizations hiring in bulk. Mesa was built for the version that's emerging. A curriculum centered on real business-building, founder collaboration, and the skills that actually matter when companies are small and execution is everything; launching products, understanding customers, generating revenue, and making decisions without a playbook. Cohort 2028 applications are open. Explore the program. Script: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Naval Ravi Khan. I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become the 10,001th employee in our MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95 percent of jobs in MNC are going to be taken away by AI. And what that means is, theoretically speaking, there are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain. Either you become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from zero to one, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product. And this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision making in startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. If you are somebody who's interested, then Mesa is still accepting applications. Apply as quickly as possible.

“I spent two years preparing for UPSC.”
Video ad, person to camera. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: customer. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Be part of Mesa's next cohort She started her career at KPMG and wanted to work in startups, but had no idea how to make the switch. At Mesa, Apoorva built an AI agent that could find influencers, track their engagement and automate personalised outreach. That agent led her to the founder of GoDesi. Today, she's an EiR at GoDesi, working directly with the founder. Script: I spent two years preparing for UPSC. Today, I worked directly with the founder of a fast-growing F&B startup. I started my career at KPMG and then decided to join Mesa School of Business. I always wanted to work in the F&B industry, but I had no idea how to meet that transition. During my 12 months at Mesa, I got to build two businesses of my own. Worked on real business problems with two brothers' organic farms, where I worked on influencer marketing for the US market. And here's the interesting part. Before Mesa, I was someone who was genuinely scared of technology. But during my time at Mesa, I built an AI agent that could identify relevant influencers, track their engagement numbers, and automate personalized outreach. And this AI agent got me an interview with the founder of Prodacy. Today, I work as an AIR at Prodacy, where I manage multiple product categories across quick commerce platforms. So, I'm preparing for UPSC to building AI automations and working directly with a startup founder. That's how much my career pivoted in just 12 months. If you're looking to make a similar career switch and work in high-impact roles at India's top startups, explore Mesa's 12-month PGP in startup leadership. Apply now.

“Only 0.001% of people have actually built something useful using AI.”
Video ad, person to camera. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Non-tech doesn't mean non-builder AI is woven into every course at Mesa with 150+ hours of applied curriculum built around one goal: every student builds at least one real, working AI product before they graduate. Not a demo. Not a prototype. Something that actually works. The window to be an early builder, not just an early learner - is still open. Explore the PG program. Get the details. Script: Only 0.001% of people have actually built something useful using AI. And this is after knowing that AI is the number one skill to learn right now. Why is it that this gap is so massive? Because most people think it's too technical for them. Because there are thousands of tools and nobody knows what to use when. Because they've watched tutorials, but they've never sat down to think about what should I do with those tutorials. And because even the few who start don't have anyone to guide them through the finish line. Mesa solves exactly this. AI is in the separate module here. It's woven into every single course. 150 plus hours of applied AI curriculum. And every student builds at least one real AI product before they graduate. Not a demo, not a toy project, something that works. For example, one of our students, an investment banker with zero tech background. Built a voice first AI companion, pitched it to 50 plus VCs, scaled it to 1000 plus monthly active users. Another one built an AI powered tool that got him his dream job. Another pivoted entirely into AI and is now leading an AI product at a fast growing startup. The gap right now isn't between people who understand AI and people who don't. It's between people who have built with AI and people who haven't. Mesa, make sure you're on the right side of that gap.

“You will be the average of the five people around you.”
Video ad, person to camera. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 13 versions. Opens with: calls out an audience. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Find Your Tribe of Business Builders at Mesa At 17 or 18, the people around you can shape how you think, what you attempt and how far you push yourself. Mesa brings together students who are already building companies, launching products and taking ideas into the real world. The result is a peer group that challenges you to think bigger from Day 1. Apply now for Mesa’s UG Program. Script: You will be the average of the five people around you and that's why Peer Group matters so much when you are 17, 18 years old. The UG cohort here at Mesa consists of extraordinary students. We have somebody who is pitched on Shark Tank and is now in Foundry which is the incubator started by Nikhil Kamar. We have a student who has gotten a 2 crore grant from Silicon Valley incubator called Entrepreneurs Force. We have three students who have built a Khakra brand doing 25 lakh in revenue every single month and we have at least five students who have launched their tech apps on the US App Store and are earning in dollars. Now how do we manage to get the best students? When we are creating the undergraduate cohort less than 5% of the applicants get an offer from Mesa. We filter for intent, hunger, willingness to learn, energy, aptitude and have a five step admissions process that involves an online test, group discussion, an AI case study interview, multiple interviews with CXOs. That's why the environment here at Mesa is extraordinary. If you are interested, apply now. Music

“Three of our first year students just pitched to Elevation Capital.”

Script: Three of our first year students just pitched to Elevation Capital. It was not a mock pitch, not a case study, a live pitch. To a $2 billion fund for a product that they built called Capture. Two of them had zero tech background. They used Claude Cote, Mesa's AI mentors and a hackathon to ship it. That is not the ceiling here. That is the baseline. At Mesa, Antler, Titan Capital, Campus Fund and Elevation Capital are not names on a guest list. They are funds looking at what students are building. Think about what that means if you are 17 years old. Most people spend their entire 20s trying to get into a room with investors. Our students are in that room before you turn 19. Not because they have networked their way in, but because they've built something worth presenting. If this is how you envision yourself spending the next three years, then you should apply for Mesa's undergraduate program in Business and Ones Connection.

“The actual efficient size of a company is shrinking very rapidly.”
Video ad, person to camera. 1 days live from 19 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The next decade belongs to builders Large companies are becoming leaner, AI is automating layers of work that used to require headcount, and a growing share of opportunity is concentrating inside small, high-leverage teams, i.e. startups. Most business programs was built for the old version of this economy: one with stable hierarchies, predictable career ladders, and large organizations hiring in bulk. Mesa was built for the version that's emerging. A curriculum centered on real business-building, founder collaboration, and the skills that actually matter when companies are small and execution is everything; launching products, understanding customers, generating revenue, and making decisions without a playbook. Cohort 2028 applications are open. Explore the program. Script: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Nauravika and I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become a 10,000 and one employee in a MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95% of jobs in MNCs are going to be taken away by AI and what that means is theoretically speaking. There are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain either. You become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Now both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from 0 to 1, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product and this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision-making startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs, where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. If you are somebody who's interested then Mesa is still accepting applications, apply as quickly as possible.

Script: If you are 25 years old, the worst thing you can do is work in a back-end role in a large army. You will be running a repetitive process. You will not be talking to customers. You will not be working with experienced leaders. In a nutshell, you are falling behind. And in the end, AI will take over most of these roles. In startup, it's the exact opposite. You will get to make decisions. You will talk to customers directly and learn how to sell. You will work with senior founders who will mentally. You will learn AI. Beat your competition. And you will get chances to make mistakes. Just ask me. Only way to learn. You will fail fast, learn fast and grow fast. This is exactly what Master School of Business is built for. It will help you break into top roles in great startups in India. You will learn directly from more than 200 founders, operators and VCs. You will work on live startup problem statements with them. You will be building real businesses and generating real revenue of more than 5 lakhs. If you want to break out of the MLC trap, then apply to Master School now.

“In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product.”
Video ad, scene or story. 10 days live from 9 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: expert or staff. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The only B-school teaching AI agents & no-code At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. This is the business school for builders. Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort. Script: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

Almost 40% of our students get jobs through this medium which is founders coming on campus and getting impressed. Which I find incredible.

“Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know.”

Developer? Learn the business side A software developer with 10 years at top tech companies feels stuck. AI is automating more of his code, and moving into product or business means proving new skills. The fix: learn how a business runs, make real revenue from scratch, meet people in leadership roles and learn to build products, not just code. Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, covers all four in 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know. He's been in coding for 10 years, has worked for top companies, fang, startups, solving their most technical problems. He was telling me the other day that he feels stuck. AI is automating the code completely. So tomorrow, if he has to move to say product or business, he will not be able to justify his salary. So what does a person like this do? The number one, this person needs to invest time in learning basics of business, business models, P&Ls, unit economics. Number two, learn to do real revenue from scratch. Pick a D2C product, brand it, package it, manage suppliers, manage inventory, sell it online, build a website, do real sales, offline if required. Number three, network. Meet more people from diverse areas. Meet people who are in leadership positions. They can open doors for you that otherwise could not be opened. And number four, learn to build with AI. I know you're technical, but solving a problem someone asked you to solve within a technical framework is very different from building a tech product from scratch. Software developers specifically are naturally analytical and great at problem solving. So if they do these four things, they are sorted for the post-AI era of work.

“90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level.”

Grow beyond one function Most mid-career professionals don't stall for lack of talent. They stall because they've only ever done one thing. The fix, in four steps: 1. Learn the basics: business models, P&Ls, unit economics 2. Build something: pick a product, package it, sell it 3. Meet people who are where you want to be 4. Learn to build with AI Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, puts all four into 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: 90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level. They are not able to pivot into roles that they like and are not considered leadership material. And you know why? It's because they've gone too deep into just doing one thing throughout their careers and they know nothing besides that. It's the biggest mistake that 27 to 32 year olds usually make. So my advice to them is, number one, they need to learn the basics of business, business models. You need to learn PNL, unit economics. Number two, learn how to start something from zero to one. Pick a problem, pick a product, package it, brand it, build a website, do actual sales. Number three, meet more people, network a lot. I know the word networking is thrown around a lot, but it's more about quality discussions with people who come from diverse backgrounds who are in positions. You want to be in. And these people can then open doors for you that you felt were impossible to open. Number four, learn to build things with AI. That is the only way you're going to stay relevant. That is the only way you can keep adding 10x value to a company and to yourself. The regular working professional, 100% going to become irrelevant if they don't do these things.

“So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make?”
Video ad, scene or story. 7 days live from 12 Nov, 4 versions. Opens with: question. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The #1 mistake mid-career pros make The biggest career mistake isn't a bad job. It's getting paid to do one narrow thing for years. Accounting, finance, data, marketing, coding, sales: AI is getting good at narrow tasks. The roles higher up need people who understand the whole business, from P&Ls to customers, partnerships and teams. Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, helps you go wide in 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make? So I'm talking about 27 to 32 year olds in a good job. The biggest mistake is the company they are working for is paying them to do one very specific task. Could be accounting, finance, data analysis, marketing, coding, sales, very narrow, very specific. So people restrict themselves to learning about just one thing and they keep going deeper just into one thing. Now what happens when AI comes in is that today, Claude can do accounting better than the best accountants in the world. So all the expertise you have accumulated stands for nothing. And as you go higher up in a hierarchy of a company, it requires people who are horizontal with their expertise. People who know businesses, they understand PNLs, they can build product, they can do sales, they can talk to customers, they can do partnerships, they can build teams, they can manage people. But unfortunately, these people don't end up learning these things. So my advice is simple. Learn to build solutions and products with AI. Learn basics of business like business models, basic PNL. Learn sales and entrepreneurship. Learn to learn something. Sell it and these can be game changers for their careers.

“In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product.”
Video ad, scene or story. 3 days live from 16 Nov, 4 versions. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: expert or staff. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The only B-school teaching AI agents & no-code At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. This is the business school for builders. Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort. Script: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

“Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know.”
Video ad, scene or story. 2 days live from 17 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Developer? Learn the business side A software developer with 10 years at top tech companies feels stuck. AI is automating more of his code, and moving into product or business means proving new skills. The fix: learn how a business runs, make real revenue from scratch, meet people in leadership roles and learn to build products, not just code. Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, covers all four in 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know. He's been in coding for 10 years, has worked for top companies, fang, startups, solving their most technical problems. He was telling me the other day that he feels stuck. AI is automating the code completely. So tomorrow, if he has to move to say product or business, he will not be able to justify his salary. So what does a person like this do? The number one, this person needs to invest time in learning basics of business, business models, P&Ls, unit economics. Number two, learn to do real revenue from scratch. Pick a D2C product, brand it, package it, manage suppliers, manage inventory, sell it online, build a website, do real sales, offline if required. Number three, network. Meet more people from diverse areas. Meet people who are in leadership positions. They can open doors for you that otherwise could not be opened. And number four, learn to build with AI. I know you're technical, but solving a problem someone asked you to solve within a technical framework is very different from building a tech product from scratch. Software developers specifically are naturally analytical and great at problem solving. So if they do these four things, they are sorted for the post-AI era of work.

“90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level.”
Video ad, scene or story. 2 days live from 17 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Grow beyond one function Most mid-career professionals don't stall for lack of talent. They stall because they've only ever done one thing. The fix, in four steps: 1. Learn the basics: business models, P&Ls, unit economics 2. Build something: pick a product, package it, sell it 3. Meet people who are where you want to be 4. Learn to build with AI Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, puts all four into 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: 90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level. They are not able to pivot into roles that they like and are not considered leadership material. And you know why? It's because they've gone too deep into just doing one thing throughout their careers and they know nothing besides that. It's the biggest mistake that 27 to 32 year olds usually make. So my advice to them is, number one, they need to learn the basics of business, business models. You need to learn PNL, unit economics. Number two, learn how to start something from zero to one. Pick a problem, pick a product, package it, brand it, build a website, do actual sales. Number three, meet more people, network a lot. I know the word networking is thrown around a lot, but it's more about quality discussions with people who come from diverse backgrounds who are in positions. You want to be in. And these people can then open doors for you that you felt were impossible to open. Number four, learn to build things with AI. That is the only way you're going to stay relevant. That is the only way you can keep adding 10x value to a company and to yourself. The regular working professional, 100% going to become irrelevant if they don't do these things.

“So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make?”
Video ad, scene or story. 2 days live from 17 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: question. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The #1 mistake mid-career pros make The biggest career mistake isn't a bad job. It's getting paid to do one narrow thing for years. Accounting, finance, data, marketing, coding, sales: AI is getting good at narrow tasks. The roles higher up need people who understand the whole business, from P&Ls to customers, partnerships and teams. Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, helps you go wide in 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now. Script: So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make? So I'm talking about 27 to 32 year olds in a good job. The biggest mistake is the company they are working for is paying them to do one very specific task. Could be accounting, finance, data analysis, marketing, coding, sales, very narrow, very specific. So people restrict themselves to learning about just one thing and they keep going deeper just into one thing. Now what happens when AI comes in is that today, Claude can do accounting better than the best accountants in the world. So all the expertise you have accumulated stands for nothing. And as you go higher up in a hierarchy of a company, it requires people who are horizontal with their expertise. People who know businesses, they understand PNLs, they can build product, they can do sales, they can talk to customers, they can do partnerships, they can build teams, they can manage people. But unfortunately, these people don't end up learning these things. So my advice is simple. Learn to build solutions and products with AI. Learn basics of business like business models, basic PNL. Learn sales and entrepreneurship. Learn to learn something. Sell it and these can be game changers for their careers.

“In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product.”
Video ad, scene or story. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: expert or staff. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The only B-school teaching AI agents & no-code At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. This is the business school for builders. Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort. Script: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

You can go to your App Store and download it. You can use it when running. And as you run, you capture territories in the real world. It's so cool. It has thousands of users using it and definitely has the potential to go viral. But here's the thing that I wanted to point out. Both of these students came from a non-technical background. They came to Mesa, underwent Mesa's AI curriculum, participated in multiple hackathons that were conducted by open AI, Anthropic, Emergent, worked with Mesa's AI mentors and used Claude Cote to build this from scratch. Now, this is exactly what is needed in India. Today's 17-18 year olds need to build things using AI tools. And yet, there is no BBA college which even has an AI curriculum. It's absolutely shocking. Education in India needs to change immediately. Else we are going to create graduates that are absolutely useless.

“As a student, imagine getting a chance to be in a meeting room with 100 plus founders.”

The B-school built for builders Mesa is selecting 200 ambitious individuals for a transformative year of startup leadership. You'll be trained by founders, business leaders, and VCs through: - a new-age curriculum, - live projects with real startups, - hands-on experience building your own ventures from scratch. Graduate ready to either launch your own company or step into leadership roles at high-growth startups. Apply to Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership now. Script: As a student, imagine getting a chance to be in a meeting room with 100 plus founders who have built successful startups during the 12 month program that you are undergoing. I did a 24 month 2 year MBA during that entire tenure at Kellogg. I probably saw two CEOs and that two from afar. I know for a fact that it changes how students live. We here at Mesa have also built a smart model around how to engage with founders. We just don't do fyside chats, those are boring. We speak to founders, understand the problems their startups are facing and we write cases about them. Students solve these cases, present their findings to the founders, there are debates, there are discussions and hence the interaction also becomes very very very interesting. Many of these founders recruit students from us. Somebody does well in the case, they get straight a job offer or an internship offer. Almost 40% of our students get jobs through this medium which is founders coming on campus and getting impressed. Which I find incredible.

“You know, Mesa incubated startups, which are startups that are built by students, have now done 50 crore plus in ARR.”
Video ad, scene or story. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: other. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Your classmates could be your co-founders From MNC managers to ex-founders to first-time builders. Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership is built for professionals who want to build, and make an impact. Apply now. Script: You know, Mesa incubated startups, which are startups that are built by students have now done 50 crore plus in ERR. This is the real revenue that we are talking about. Together they have raised more than 25 crore in funding. There are two students who have been on Shark Tank. There are also a few more in the pipeline and you will be seeing them live on Shark Tank very soon. But the point here is that we invest a lot in entrepreneurship resources. For example, there is very strict guidance on how to pick an idea. What is it that you are going to be building? It's probably the most important thing that you need to learn and that's where most people get stuck. One-on-one mentorship from proven founders, grants up to Rs.10 lakh, a dedicated team that supports your building journey which might be very different from somebody else's building journey. Demo days where you get to pitch to 50 plus VCs, partnerships with 10 plus international incubators. And another thing besides all of these resources that I give credit to is our pedagogy. Where in just the first 8 weeks, every single student does 5 lakh in sales. Whether you are building a business, whether you are in careers, whatever it is you have to do this. You have to pick a product, you have to build a website, you have to package it, you have to brand it, to create social media content, run performance marketing, sell online, sell offline. It builds the mindset and muscle required to be a successful entrepreneur. That's exactly what we are trying to do here at Mesa. Thank you.

“Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know.”
Video ad, scene or story. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: story opening. Offer: none. On screen: unnamed presenter. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

Engineers: Learn the Business Side You're a software engineer. AI is automating more of your work. What do you do next? At Mesa, you learn the 4 things that matter now: → The basics of business: business models and P&Ls → How to make real revenue from scratch → A network of people who can open doors for you → How to build a tech product from scratch with AI PGP in Startup Leadership & Entrepreneurship. Apply now. Script: Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know. He's been in coding for 10 years, has worked for top companies, fang, startups, solving their most technical problems. He was telling me the other day that he feels stuck. AI is automating the code completely. So tomorrow if he has to move to say product or business, he will not be able to justify his salary. So what does a person like this do? The number one, this person needs to invest time in learning basics of business, business model, PNL, unit economics. Number two, learn to do real revenue from scratch. Pick a D2C product, brand it, package it, manage suppliers, manage inventory, sell it online, build a website, do real sales, offline if required. Number three, network. Meet more people from diverse areas. Meet people who are in leadership positions. They can open doors for you that otherwise could not be opened. And number four, learn to build with AI. I know you're technical, but solving a problem someone asked you to solve within a technical framework is very different from building a tech product from scratch. Software developers specifically are naturally analytical and great at problems only. So if they do these four things, they are sorted for the post AI era of work.

“In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product.”
Video ad, scene or story. 1 days live from 18 Nov, 1 version. Opens with: number or claim. Offer: none. On screen: expert or staff. Language: English. Button goes to: website. Ad Library
Ad text and script

The only B-school teaching AI agents & no-code At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. This is the business school for builders. Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort. Script: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

“I don't know how many people know this, but we have professors from M7 business schools teaching at Mesa.”

The B-school built for builders Mesa is selecting 200 ambitious individuals for a transformative year of startup leadership. You'll be trained by founders, business leaders, and VCs through: - a new-age curriculum, - live projects with real startups, - hands-on experience building your own ventures from scratch. Graduate ready to either launch your own company or step into leadership roles at high-growth startups. Apply to Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership now. Script: I don't know how many people know this but we have professors from M7 Business Schools teaching at Pesna. M7 Business Schools are the top 7 Business Schools in the US. I'll give you an example. So there is this professor called Tim Corkins. He's from the Kellogg School of Management. He's considered to be the best professor in the world for marketing and brand. He teaches also at Kellogg which is supposed to be the best marketing school in the world. Now when he comes to India he teaches only at one Business School method. And he flies down every year from the US. He doesn't need to of course but he still does it. So I asked him one day you know why do you do this every year? You fly to India and UTC students and he told me that the very the perspectives, the depth of the perspectives that he gets from MESSA students. He doesn't get anywhere. The energy here is insane and he loves debating on marketing strategies. And of course one of the biggest things that he does here that he loves doing is this thing called the IPL ad review. For those of you who don't know, the IPL ad review is a session where you look at all the ads that have been produced by different brands for IPL that year. And those are reviewed by marketing geniuses from India along with Professor Balkkin's framework of how to look at ads. It's just an example of the quality of teaching that happened here at Fançon.

Engineers: Learn the Business Side You're a software engineer. AI is automating more of your work. What do you do next? At Mesa, you learn the 4 things that matter now: → The basics of business: business models and P&Ls → How to make real revenue from scratch → A network of people who can open doors for you → How to build a tech product from scratch with AI PGP in Startup Leadership & Entrepreneurship. Apply now. Script: Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know. He's been in coding for 10 years, has worked for top companies, fang, startups, solving their most technical problems. He was telling me the other day that he feels stuck. AI is automating the code completely. So tomorrow if he has to move to say product or business, he will not be able to justify his salary. So what does a person like this do? The number one, this person needs to invest time in learning basics of business, business model, PNL, unit economics. Number two, learn to do real revenue from scratch. Pick a D2C product, brand it, package it, manage suppliers, manage inventory, sell it online, build a website, do real sales, offline if required. Number three, network. Meet more people from diverse areas. Meet people who are in leadership positions. They can open doors for you that otherwise could not be opened. And number four, learn to build with AI. I know you're technical, but solving a problem someone asked you to solve within a technical framework is very different from building a tech product from scratch. Software developers specifically are naturally analytical and great at problems only. So if they do these four things, they are sorted for the post AI era of work.

Script: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number.
